goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: XSS via unsanitized `raw_html` cook method in `app/models/post.rb:131` — `cook` method returns `raw` directly for `raw_html` posts with no sanitization, allowing malicious scripts from external RSS feeds to execute in readers' browsers

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff adds a new `Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw` when `cook_method` is `raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook`). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts from external RSS/remote content with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and passes `contents`/`doc.content` (from RSS via `SimpleRSS.parse` and from HTTP via `ruby-readability`) into `PostCreator` with `skip_validations: true`. There is no sanitization step before saving, and the embed view renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so any HTML/JS that makes it into `raw` (including potentially `<script>` or event-handler attributes, or attribute injection via the interpolated `url` inside `<a href='#{url}'>`) will execute in users' browsers under the Discourse origin. This is a verifiable XSS risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: XSS in imported_from footer in `app/models/topic_embed.rb:10` — URL is interpolated directly into HTML without escaping, allowing injection of arbitrary HTML/JS via crafted URLs

adjudication.rationale:
Real issue. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends HTML directly to `contents`: ```rb contents << "\n
\n#{I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")}\n" ``` `url` is interpolated into an HTML attribute and body without escaping. The only validation is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent characters like a single quote (`'`) that can break out of `href='...'` and inject arbitrary attributes/JS (e.g., `http://example.com/' onclick='alert(1)`). Since imported posts are created with `cook_method: :raw_html` and `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged for that mode, this injected HTML would be rendered verbatim (and the embed view uses `raw post.cooked`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `Kernel#open` used with external URLs in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:28` and `app/models/topic_embed.rb:48` — can execute shell commands with `|` prefix, should use `URI.open` or `OpenURI.open_uri` instead
`force: true` added to existing migration in `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3` — will DROP the `top_topics` table and all data if migration is re-run

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. While `force: true` does drop the table if it already exists, Rails migrations are normally executed exactly once per database (tracked in `schema_migrations`), so this change will not drop data during a normal `db:migrate` on an already-migrated DB. On a fresh DB the table doesn’t exist yet, so `force: true` has no effect. The finding’s scenario (“if migration is re-run”) is not a verifiable defect introduced in typical operation based on this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tabnabbing via `target: '_blank'` without `rel: 'noopener'` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb:4,7,20,24` — opened tab can access `window.opener` and redirect original page

adjudication.rationale: In app/views/embed/best.html.erb the diff introduces several `link_to(..., target: '_blank')` links (header buttons and per-post links) without adding `rel: 'noopener'` (or `noopener noreferrer`). By default, opening a new tab/window this way allows the opened page to access `window.opener`, which is the classic reverse-tabnabbing vector. There is no mitigation shown in the diff (no `rel` attribute, no JS `noopener` handling).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `postMessage` with potentially nil/empty origin in `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:10` — nil `request.referer` renders as empty string causing `SyntaxError` in browsers

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb`, the `ensure_embeddable` before_filter rejects requests with a missing referer (`URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`), and the controller spec explicitly expects failure when there is no referer. So `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb` should not be rendered with `request.referer == nil` in normal execution. Also, even if it were nil, ERB would interpolate to an empty string and `parent.postMessage(..., '')` would be a runtime DOMException/invalid targetOrigin error, not a JavaScript parse `SyntaxError` as claimed. Therefore the finding (nil/empty origin causing SyntaxError) is not a verifiable problem introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No timeout on HTTP requests in `app/models/topic_embed.rb:48` and `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:28` — slow or unresponsive remote server will hang the job indefinitely

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces remote fetches via `open-uri` without specifying `open_timeout`/`read_timeout`: `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` and `open(url).read` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (`app/models/topic_embed.rb`). This is verifiable in the added code. Without explicit timeouts, these calls can block the scheduled job/worker thread for a long time (and depending on Ruby/Net::HTTP defaults and network conditions, potentially indefinitely), so the reliability concern is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `i.content` may be nil in RSS feed in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35` — not all RSS/Atom items have a `content` field, causing `NoMethodError` on nil
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag the same underlying problem: RSS/Atom items may not have a populated `content` field, so calling methods on `i.content` can raise a nil-related exception (`NoMethodError`). The golden adds a specific mitigation (fallback to `description`), but the core issue identified is the same.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cache duration too long for loading state in `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:20` — 1-minute cache means user may see loading page for up to 60 seconds even after topic is created

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is executed unconditionally (after either rendering `loading` or building `@topic_view`). When no topic exists, the action renders the `loading` template, which includes JS to reload after 30 seconds. However, the 1-minute cache headers set by `discourse_expires_in` can cause the browser/proxy to serve the cached loading response on reload, meaning the user may continue seeing the loading page even after the topic is created until the cache TTL expires. This is a directly verifiable mismatch in the diff between the intended reload behavior and the caching policy.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `feed_key` method defined but never used in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:18-20` — dead code that should be removed or implemented

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the `feed_key` method is defined (lines shown in diff: `def feed_key ... end`) but there are no references to `feed_key` anywhere else in that file (e.g., `execute` only calls `poll_feed`, and `poll_feed` parses and imports items directly). Within the provided diff, the method is unused, making it dead code as the finding claims.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test coverage for actual feed parsing in `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` — only gating conditions tested, actual feed parsing and item extraction untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces non-trivial feed parsing logic in `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` (uses `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`, iterates `rss.items`, derives `url` from `i.link`/`i.id`, unescapes/scrubs content, and calls `TopicEmbed.import`). However, `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only tests the gating conditions in `execute` and that `poll_feed` is delegated to; it contains no tests that stub `open`/`SimpleRSS.parse` or assert correct item extraction/handling and calls to `TopicEmbed.import`. This lack of coverage for the core parsing/import behavior is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Breaking change in Disqus import — removed `:category` option in `lib/tasks/disqus.thor:117` without documentation or deprecation

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `method_option :category` and the associated `category_id` handling in `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, so the Disqus import CLI no longer supports selecting a category. However, calling this a “REAL problem” is not strictly verifiable from the diff: it could be an intentional interface change (the import behavior is also fundamentally changed to `TopicEmbed.import_remote`), and the claim “without documentation or deprecation” cannot be confirmed from the provided changeset alone (no docs/changelog context is shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Deleted user not handled in embed view in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb:17-18` — `post.user.small_avatar_url` and `post.user.username` will raise `NoMethodError` if user has been deleted

adjudication.rationale: The embed view directly calls `post.user.small_avatar_url` and `post.user.username`, but the diff does not show any scenario where `post.user` can be `nil`. In Discourse/Rails, `posts` typically have a non-null `user_id` and user “deletion” is commonly handled via anonymization/disable rather than removing the row (or posts are removed with the user), so the proposed `NoMethodError` relies on an external assumption (hard-deleted user record while post remains). That makes this finding speculative and not verifiably a real problem from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inline synchronous execution of `PollFeed` job in `lib/topic_retriever.rb:39` — synchronously polls entire RSS feed inline, blocking the job and processing all feed items instead of just the requested URL

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `lib/topic_retriever.rb` inside `perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it directly calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline (synchronously) before proceeding. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` parses the configured feed and iterates `rss.items.each`, importing every item via `TopicEmbed.import(...)`, not just the single `@embed_url` being retrieved. This can significantly increase work/latency for a single embed retrieval (and has side effects of importing many topics) and is verifiably present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing newline at end of file in `embed.css.scss`, `loading.html.erb`, `layouts/embed.html.erb`, `topic_retriever.rb`

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly shows “\ No newline at end of file” for `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss`, `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`, `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb`, and `lib/topic_retriever.rb`, so the observation is factually correct. However, a missing trailing newline is a formatting/style nit and not a bug, security issue, or correctness defect introduced by the change (and it’s also present in at least one other file in the diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unnecessary whitespace changes in existing files `db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` and `lib/post_revisor.rb:14` — pollute diff without functional value

adjudication.rationale: The diff does include whitespace-only changes: in `db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` a trailing space is removed and the file now lacks a trailing newline (`\ No newline at end of file`), and in `lib/post_revisor.rb` a blank line is removed. However, these are formatting/style nits that do not introduce a bug, security issue, or correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `document['body']` instead of `document.body` in `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11` — bracket notation is unusual for property access

adjudication.rationale: In app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb the code uses `document['body'].offsetHeight`. In JavaScript, bracket notation for property access is equivalent to dot notation (`document.body`) when the property name is a valid identifier like `body`. This is unusual but still correct and should work the same in browsers; it does not introduce a functional bug, security issue, or correctness defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `discourseUrl` trailing slash assumption in `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:7` — malformed URL if embedding site doesn't include trailing slash

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, `iframe.src` is built via string concatenation: `discourseUrl + "embed/best?..."`. There is no normalization to ensure `discourseUrl` ends with `/`, so if `discourseUrl` is provided as a typical base URL like `https://forum.example.com` (no trailing slash), the result becomes `https://forum.example.comembed/best?...`, which is an invalid path/host. The diff contains no code that enforces/normalizes the trailing slash for `discourseUrl`, so this is a real correctness issue introduced by the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Port handling in `absolutize_urls` in `app/models/topic_embed.rb:64` — condition doesn't consider scheme-port mismatches, e.g., `http://example.com:443/` would incorrectly omit the port

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, the prefix appends `:#{uri.port}` only when `uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443`. This treats 80 and 443 as “always default” regardless of scheme. For example, `URI('http://example.com:443').port` is 443, so the code will omit the port and produce `http://example.com/...` instead of `http://example.com:443/...`. Same issue for `https://example.com:80`. That’s a real correctness bug in the diff affecting relative URL absolutization for scheme/port mismatches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test assertions in `after` block in `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:37-40` — unconventional and can produce confusing failure messages

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`, the `after` hook inside the `context "success"` unconditionally asserts `response.should be_success` and `X-Frame-Options` for each example in that context. This is unconventional test structure, but it is not a correctness bug in the code under test nor a verifiable defect introduced by the diff. At most it’s a style/maintainability nit (potentially adding an additional failure if an example fails before setting a successful response), which the instructions classify as not a “real problem.”
